**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless a “Reverse” card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color cards; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. First to reach the agreed‑upon point total (usually 500) wins the game. | | **Special Rules** | • **Uno Call** – When you have one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and someone catches you, you must draw two cards.
• **Challenge** – If you suspect a player illegally played a Wild Draw Four, you can challenge them. If they were right, you draw four cards; if they were wrong, you draw six. | | **Variations** | Many house rules exist (e.g., “Stacking” where +2 or +4 cards can be stacked, “No Challenge” rules, etc.). Clarify before starting. | **Quick Tips** 1. Keep track of the current color; it’s the easiest way to decide what to play. 2. Use action cards strategically—save a “Draw Two” for when you’re about to win. 3. Remember to shout “UNO!” when you’re down to one card. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
